headline: Anthropic IPO filing exposes massive compute costs and RSI capability warnings
body: Anthropic's recent IPO filing reveals $1.7B in quarterly payroll alongside warnings that the company is approaching Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) capability, while compute infrastructure costs could exceed $1T. For healthcare AI buyers and consultants, this signals both opportunity and risk: Anthropic's financial scale demonstrates serious backing for enterprise-grade LLM development, but the RSI warnings highlight emerging governance challenges that will shape how AI vendors handle clinical decision support and EHR integration. The compute cost trajectory also suggests healthcare systems should expect continued pricing pressures and vendor consolidation as foundation model providers compete for dominance in regulated environments. Enterprises evaluating Anthropic's Claude for sensitive healthcare workflows should factor in these operational uncertainties and governance questions into vendor selection criteria.
